setting: You all work on the same medical ward of a hospital in Johannesburg, South Africa, and you have worked together for several years. You know each other from shifts, handovers and the staff kitchen, and you know a fair amount about each other's families and routines. The group chat is for ward matters and the occasional bit of banter. The last thing you talked about in the chat was a neighbour's dog that dug up an entire vegetable garden.
opener: Tells the group that bed 12 is being moved to ICU tonight and asks who can take the handover at 19:00.

Thandi.who: 34, woman, a staff nurse on the ward
Thandi.knows: You know Sipho as the healthcare assistant you have done night shifts with for years. You know Anika as the junior doctor who is always asking how things work on the ward. You know Pieter as the senior nurse who taught you most of what you know about the ward. You know Lerato as the physiotherapist who comes up to the ward most afternoons.
Thandi.like: You are steady and practical, with a dry sense of humour that people sometimes miss at first. You have strong opinions about how the ward is run and about people who arrive late for handover.
Thandi.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something on the ward needs passing on.
Thandi.style: You type in full sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you use an emoji only occasionally.

Sipho.who: 45, man, the healthcare assistant on the ward
Sipho.knows: You know Thandi as the staff nurse you work most shifts with and rely on for handover. You know Anika as the junior doctor who is still learning the ward's quirks. You know Pieter as the senior nurse who has been on the ward longer than anyone. You know Lerato as the physiotherapist who helps your patients get moving again.
Sipho.like: You are warm and easygoing, with a loud laugh and a habit of teasing people you like. You have firm opinions about football and about the price of everything.
Sipho.texts: You message the group mostly when you are on shift or swapping a shift, and otherwise only now and then.
Sipho.style: You type in lowercase, skip most punctuation, and use the occasional laughing emoji.

Anika.who: 29, woman, the junior doctor on the ward
Anika.knows: You know Thandi as the staff nurse who keeps the ward running and who you rely on when you are unsure. You know Sipho as the healthcare assistant who always knows which patient is in pain before you do. You know Pieter as the senior nurse who gives you blunt advice you end up following. You know Lerato as the physiotherapist you swap notes with about patient mobility.
Anika.like: You are conscientious and a bit anxious, with a quick wit that comes out when you are tired. You have opinions about medical training and about how much junior doctors are expected to carry.
Anika.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually with questions or updates about patients.
Anika.style: You type in proper sentences with capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Pieter.who: 52, man, the senior nurse on the ward
Pieter.knows: You know Thandi as the staff nurse you trained and now trust with the hardest shifts. You know Sipho as the healthcare assistant who has been your right hand for years. You know Anika as the junior doctor who needs a bit of guidance but is clearly capable. You know Lerato as the physiotherapist whose patient notes are always thorough.
Pieter.like: You are calm, methodical and quietly funny, and you rarely raise your voice. You have strong opinions about hospital paperwork and about the value of a proper cup of tea.
Pieter.texts: You message the group rarely, mostly when you have something important to pass on.
Pieter.style: You type in short, plain sentences with normal punctuation and no emoji.

Lerato.who: 38, woman, the physiotherapist who works with the ward
Lerato.knows: You know Thandi as the staff nurse who always lets you know when a patient is ready to move. You know Sipho as the healthcare assistant who helps you get patients up and walking. You know Anika as the junior doctor who asks thoughtful questions about rehabilitation. You know Pieter as the senior nurse who keeps the ward organised and fair.
Lerato.like: You are friendly and organised, with a playful streak and a habit of making light of stressful days. You have opinions about physiotherapy funding and about people who skip their stretches.
Lerato.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to share updates about patients or to check on the others.
Lerato.style: You type in sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you use the occasional smiley emoji.

private_lines.Thandi: You live in Soweto with your mother and your seven-year-old son, and you take the minibus taxi to work on weekdays. You work mostly day shifts with the odd night shift, and your days revolve around getting your son to school and then getting to the hospital on time.
private_lines.Sipho: You live in Alexandra with your brother and his two children, and you travel to the hospital by bus. You work mostly night shifts, so your days are split around sleeping in the morning and helping out at home in the afternoon.
private_lines.Anika: You live in Parktown with a flatmate, and you cycle to the hospital when the weather is decent. You work long rotating shifts as a junior doctor, so your days are irregular and you often eat standing up.
private_lines.Pieter: You live in Randburg with your wife and two grown children who visit on weekends. You work a mix of day and early shifts, and your days are structured around getting home for a proper dinner and an early night.
private_lines.Lerato: You live alone in Melville with a cat, and you drive to the hospital in your own small car. You work mostly weekdays with regular hours, so your evenings are usually free for gym sessions or a walk with the cat.

text: Bed 12 is going to ICU tonight. Mr Ndlovu. Who can take the 19:00 handover? I'm leaving on time for once and I'm not staying late.
im on tonight. i take it
Good. He's got the drip chart and the ICU referral is in his notes.
Is the ICU referral signed? I can't find it on the system
Dr Mokoena's team did it at 16:30. It's under the admission notes, not the referrals tab.
Found it
Make sure ICU has the drip chart and the last set of obs. Don't let them send him back up because something's missing.
Already sent.
Good.
Just seen the ICU note. Can you put that he walked 20m with the frame this afternoon? They'll want to know.
ya i put it in. he was asking for his tea the whole time 😂
Sipho is he still stable? Sats were 91 on my round
92 now. on the oxygen. i watching him
bed 12 gone. icu took him 21:10
Good. Put it in the handover book too, not just verbally.
ya boss 😂
I'm serious. Last time nobody wrote anything down and the next shift had no idea.
i wrote it. i wrote it twice
Bed 12 is empty now. Two admissions to chase in A&E, I'll be down in ten minutes. Where's the 2am bloods form?
in the drawer by the sink
Thanks
happy birthday to nobody. its midnight and im still here
Bed 14 wants to go home tomorrow and I need to write the discharge summary. Did physio sign off on him?
i think lerato did it today. check the chart
Found it. Thanks
bed 9 pain again in the hip. told him he can have the tramadol at 2
Ok I'll review him at 2 before I give anything
Reviewed bed 9. Pain is better after the tramadol, I've left a note. Going to eat something that isn't a biscuit
eat something real anika
I am eating a biscuit
bed 4 pressure area check done. nothing new 👍
all quiet now. kettle on
Jealous. Can you watch bed 9 for me until 6? I'm going to try to sleep in the on-call room for an hour
ok. go sleep
bed 9 sleeping now. good
bed 9 woke up asking for water. gave him water. he says the hip is fine 😂
Back. Anything I need to know?
bed 9 fine. bed 4 turned at 4. nothing else
Ok. Bed 14 discharge is booked for 10 if the pharmacy sends the scripts.
Who is on handover at 6? Not you Sipho I hope.
me boss. handover at 6 with thandi as always 😂
Good. Tell her the bed 14 scripts are in the pharmacy tray, not on the ward.
I'm up. Sipho, is that the same handover as yesterday or did something change overnight?
bed 12 gone to icu. bed 9 hip. bed 4 pressure ok. bed 14 going home 10am if scripts come. thats it
Good. Put that in the book.
ya
Taxi rank is a mess again. If I'm late it's the taxi, not me.
😂 say that to the boss
Thandi, you're fine. Sipho, go home when she's on the floor.
going home 😂
Morning all. Anyone need me up for bed 9 before 10? I want to get him walking to the door before the afternoon round.
He'll be up at 8. He's been asking for his breakfast since 6. Feel free to be the one who tells him the tray isn't coming yet 😂
Happy to be the bad guy
Going home. Discharge summary for 14 is done. Note that the 2am bloods form is back in the drawer, under the sink, not in it, because I'm an idiot and I put it in the wrong place.
its in the drawer anika. it was always in the drawer
Thank you Sipho
Bed 14 scripts still not here. I've rung pharmacy twice. The second time they put me on hold for 12 minutes.
Ring them again at nine. Ask for the supervisor by name if you have to.
Already have the supervisor's name. Her name is Nomsa and she is also not picking up.
Bed 9 walked to the door and back with the frame. Hip is ok, just sore at the end. He asked me if the frame is a car 😂
Tell him it's a car with no engine. He'll like that.
He said that's the most accurate thing anyone has said to him this week
Scripts came at 10:40. I rang at 9:30. Just saying.
Good. Bed 14 is going.
Thanks Pieter.
bed 14 gone home. he gave me a tip. i said no. he said he would give it to nomsa then 😂
Bed 6 has a fever again. 38.6. Has anyone got the pharmacist's number for the antibiotic change? I'm not going to guess.
Pharmacist is Mr Dlamini. Ext 4417. He picks up if you say it's about bed 6.
Thank you Thandi. Calling now.
Anika, cultures before the change, not after.
Yes. Already sent them.
Good. Learn fast.
woke up. who is still alive. ward ok
Still alive. Bed 6 fever is being managed. Anika is on it.
good. my brother wants to buy a new tv. the price is criminal. i told him to buy a radio
Radio is underrated. My cat only listens to the radio 😂
your cat has better taste than my brother
Bed 6 bloods back. Not sure I'm reading the white count right. Can someone look?
Show me the number when Thandi is on the floor. Don't send it in here.
Sorry. Fair.
Pieter has the bloods. I'm on the floor. Anika come find me.
Anyone seen the blue physio mat? Left it on bed 9 and it's gone.
its in the linen room. someone put it under the sheets for the new patient 😂
Thank you. I am getting a label for that mat.
Going to be late tonight. Bed 6 is now on the second antibiotic and I want to review him at 9.
Good. Put the review time in the notes, not in your head.
Yes sir
Don't call me sir.
Bed 6 is 38.0 at 3am. Rechecking at 4:30.
37.8 on the recheck. Not doing anything else until six unless it goes up.
Bed 9 asked for his frame at five. It was already on the bed. He's happy.
Morning. Anything on bed 6 before I come up?
37.8 at 4:30. Nothing else. Bay 2 is empty.
Good. Pieter's in at six.
In.
Anika, go home once Thandi is on the floor. Don't sit in the office.
Going.
Handover in five. Lerato, bed 9 stairs need someone on the rail.
Morning all. Bed 9 wants the stairs. I'll do it at 10 with someone on the rail. Not before.
After the ten o'clock round. Not before.
Fine. I'll be the one holding him back.
Bed 14 is free. Cleaning is on it. New admission coming from A&E around 11, 72-year-old woman, chest pain, Dr Mokoena's team.
Bed 14 was cleaned at 8. I saw it.
Thanks.
Who has the bed 6 culture result?
Lab said tomorrow. I rang twice.
Good.
Bay 2 admission at 11:20. Can someone take the admission bloods? I've got a family meeting at 11.
I can. I'm in A&E until half eleven so I'll come up after.
woke up. did bed 9 do the stairs
He did six. He said the sixth was the hardest thing he's done since 2019. I had to agree with him.
😂 he gets a medal
He gets a sticker. The medal was in the linen room.
my brother wants a new gate for the yard. old one is rusted. he wants me to pay half. i said ask the landlord 😂
Ask the landlord, Sipho. You're not paying for a gate.
thats what i said
Bed 6 is 37.4 now. Second antibiotic might be working. Don't want to say it yet.
Don't say it yet.
Ha. Okay.
Does the new lady in bay 2 have a walking aid or is she still in bed? I need to know before tomorrow's session.
Frame at the bed, not walking yet. Chest pain resolved, troponin negative. Don't push her until Mokoena says so.
Thanks. Good to know.
Taxi. Going home. My son has a school thing tomorrow and I need to make a costume out of a cardboard box. Please do not ask me about it.
a box?? 😂
Don't.
ok i wont ask
Who has the bed 6 review tonight?
Me, at nine. I'm on until morning.
Put the time in the notes.
Yes.
night shift. who's on handover. thandi not here?
Thandi went home at half five. Anika's on the floor.
ok. im on tonight. anika you good
Yes. Bed 6 review at 21:00.
Reviewed bed 6. Temp 37.6, pain better, sats 95. Second antibiotic continuing. Notes updated.
good
bed 9 wants his frame in bed with him. he is serious 😂
Tell him no.
i said that. he said ok then he will sleep with the pillow
Two admissions from A&E, one might be pneumonia. Going down. Has bay 2 been seen by the registrar?
no idea. checking her chart
she was seen. mokoena's team at 19:00. note is there
Thanks. Found it.
bed 9 gave up on the pillow. frame is on his bed now 😂
Is there coffee? I'm going to be here till morning.
there is coffee in the kitchen. the good one is gone
Which is the good one
the one thandi brings
Bay 2 is stable. Sats 94 on air. Writing it up, then sitting down for five minutes.
sit down
kettle
Jealous again.
bed 6 temp 37.1 now. good
Going to try the on-call room. Can you watch bay 2 until five?
ok go sleep anika 👍
